notes: BATCH AL (eye drops and mouth products). Routes: eye drops 'eye'; mouthwashes and oral gel 'oromucosal'. NO GROUP MEMBERSHIPS ADDED: all six are local products. Benzydamine (SmPC ATC M01AX07/M02AA05, 'non-steroids') was NOT added to 'nsaid', and the choline salicylate gel was NOT added to 'salicylate' or 'nsaid', so systemic NSAID/salicylate interaction rules of other medicines do not fire on them. Their own SmPC statements are expressed as rules from their side instead: choline salicylate gel -> aspirin (avoid, 'should not be used with ... aspirin or other salicylates except under the direction of a doctor') and -> group:anticoagulant (info, effect bleeding; SmPC states no action). The 'other salicylates' wording also covers the topical salicylate rubs (menthol/methyl salicylate/camphor; aescin/diethylamine salicylate) but no rule was made for those (topical-to-oral-gel pairing; integrator may add). The uricosuric interaction has no master-list partner and is shown in the section only. NO UK PRODUCT (3): (1) naphazoline/pheniramine eye drops: no UK product with pheniramine; the clinic monograph emc link (5640) is naphazoline + witch hazel, a different combination. UK single-ingredient naphazoline eye drops exist (MHRA Products, PL 18259/0009 and 0003) and the naphazoline + witch hazel SmPC contraindicates closed-angle glaucoma and MAOIs (and within 14 days of stopping) and warns about antihypertensives, cardiac glycosides, quinidine and tricyclics; this was NOT used because it does not cover pheniramine and batch precedent marks missing combinations no-uk-product. The integrator may prefer to add naphazoline-only content as a substitute. (2) polyvinyl alcohol/povidone eye drops: no UK licensed product; clinic emc links (1638, 3537) are hypromellose eye drops (different active). (3) krameria (rhatany) mouthwash: no UK SmPC/PIL/THR; clinic emc link (12348) is metronidazole tablets (wrong link). LEVEL CHOICES: chlorhexidine under-12 rule is 'avoid' ('should not use the product unless recommended by a healthcare professional', outside 4.3) - the action keeps the 'unless recommended' wording; benzydamine 12-and-under is 'avoid' (age maxYears 13: one SmPC 'should not be used in children aged 12 years or under', the other 'indicated in adults and children aged 13 years and over'); benzydamine aspirin/NSAID hypersensitivity is 'avoid' ('not advisable', 4.4); choline salicylate 4.3 items (under 16, active peptic ulceration, salicylate/aspirin/NSAID hypersensitivity, >100 mg/day salicylate in trimester 3) are 'contraindicated'. The active peptic ulcer rule uses the existing condition 'peptic-ulcer-gi-bleeding' (which also covers history); the SmPC says 'active' and the rule text says so. The trimester-3 rule keeps the SmPC's own dose wording (>100 mg/day salicylate); the SmPC gives no mg/day equivalent for the gel. CHOLINE SALICYLATE - CONFLICT BETWEEN TWO VERSIONS OF THE SAME UK SPC (PL 00063/0121): the current text on MHRA Products (revised 28/08/2026) differs from the older text still on emc (emc-624, revised 20/11/2020). Changes in 2026: (a) active peptic ulceration moved from 4.3 contraindication to 4.4 caution (active or recurring); (b) hypersensitivity line now names choline salicylate and cetalkonium; (c) pregnancy T1-T2 changed from consult doctor/dentist to should not be used unless clearly necessary, and T3 adds should not be used in the last trimester; (d) breastfeeding changed from short-term use acceptable to contraindicated. Both are kept as separate items/rules, each naming its text (peptic ulcer: contraindicated-2020 + caution-2026; T1-T2: avoid-2026 + caution-2020; breastfeeding: contraindicated-2026 rule, 2020 wording shown in section and consequence). Integrator may drop the 2020 rules once emc updates. Under-16: SmPC 4.3 (both versions) and MHRA/CHM DSU (June 2009) agree (Reye's syndrome). CHLORHEXIDINE: two near-identical UK 0.2% mouthwash SmPCs (emc-529, emc-66); MHRA DSU Jan 2012 on hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis used for the allergy rule. NOT FOUND: no BUMPS leaflet for chlorhexidine, benzydamine or choline salicylate (404); no relevant SPS breastfeeding/renal/monitoring pages (SPS search returned only unrelated pages); no NICE content used. Note: emc rate-limited (HTTP 429) several searches; all failed searches were repeated successfully with --fresh. BRAND PRESCRIBING: none stated by any UK source. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/AJ-AK-AL.md): choline salicylate now uses ONLY the current 2026 SPC; the superseded 2020 rules (peptic ulcer contraindicated, T1-T2 caution) and the 2020 section items were removed; emc-624 is cited only in the formulation note that names the superseded version. The third-trimester rule was split: contraindicated only at salicylate doses >100 mg/day (4.3, qualifier in the concern) plus a separate avoid rule (4.6: should not be used in the last trimester). Chlorhexidine pregnancy/breastfeeding info rules added. The 3 no-uk-product decisions were confirmed (emc search: no results for pheniramine, polyvinyl alcohol, krameria; naphazoline search resolves only to the naphazoline + witch hazel product).
